The purpose of this announcement is to conduct a market survey to solicit statements of interest and capabilities from interested vendors in accordance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Acquisition Management System (AMS) Policy 3.2.1.2.1. This market survey will enable the FAA to review responses that are current and will assist with acquisition planning based on the current data obtained. The responses to this market survey will be used for informational purposes only. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has a requirement for the acquisition of multiple items of test equipment using a blanket purchase agreement (BPA). Please refer to the attachment for Equipment identification and estimated annual quantities. The respondents are required to provide a list of the equipment specified in the Statement of Work (SOW) that they can supply. Procurement would be shipped to multiple government locations within and outside CONUS (Continental United States). At this time, the acquisition strategy and nature of competition have not been determined for the BPA. The Government welcomes statements of interest and capabilities from all small businesses, including service-disabled veteran-owned small business, women-owned small businesses, and 8(a) certified firms, which are capable of providing the required items. Based on historical performance, it is anticipated that contract will be set aside to Small Businesses. Depending on responses to this survey and analysis of market research collected, the Government will develop and refine its procurement strategy at its discretion, which may involve a full and open competition, a set-aside of all or part of the procurement, or pursuit of another acquisition strategy that the Government determines is in its best interest in order to fulfill its requirements. The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20, is conducting market research to identify potential sources which can provide the following services: Title: Panic and Intrusion Alarm Replacement and Monitoring NAICS Code: 561621, Security Systems Services (except Locksmiths) Locations: Fairview VA Clinic, 1800 NE Market Drive, Fairview, OR 97024 Hillsboro VA Clinic,1925 NE Stucki Ave, 3rd and 4th Floor, Hillsboro, OR, 97006 West Linn VA Clinic, 1750 SW Blankenship Road, Suite 300, West Linn, OR 97068 The Dalles CBOC, 704 Veterans Drive, The Dalles, OR 97058 Bend CBOC, 2650 NE Courtney Drive, Bend, OR, 97701 Salem CBOC, 1750 McGilchrist Street SE, Salem, OR 97302 Tasks: Within 30 days, upon award of the contract, the contractor shall remove, install, and test all new components at each location. This should include, keypads, panels, motion sensors, and wireless panic alarms, to the quantity provided at each location. Motion sensors must be based off of PIR and/or Microwave Technology. Sensors should range in detection distance of 40 to 200 feet depending on the area being covered. Some areas will require 360-degree sensors due to cross areas. Sensors should comprise of anti-masking technology where available. Once installed, Contractor shall provide alarm monitoring 24/7. All Security Systems and components must have the ability to be live tested with the monitoring station every month. This will include individual panic alarms, motion sensors, door contacts, and any other form of input. All systems must have the ability to accept multiple access codes with only one master code. The system should have the ability to track which codes were used to arm and disarm the system. The system should have the capability to be armed and disarmed with the use of a proximity card or key fob. With the possible potential to use HSPD-12 compliant ID cards, commonly known as VA PIV Badges or CAC Cards. The government should have the ability to log into the systems remotely to arm, disarm, and view activity history remotely. Contractor shall reply to repair requests within 4 hours of call. All repairs must be completed within 5 days. The United States Department Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), supported by the R8 Procurement and Property Support Services Division, Region 8 US Forest Service, CSA 11, intends to award on a single source basis. Purchase order type will be a Firm Fixed Price awarded to Alleghany Farm Services. This requirement is for the purchase of professional agricultural drainage construction services to install, repair, and improve subsurface drainage tile systems at the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), Plant Genetic Resources Unit located at 2862 County Road 6, Geneva, New York 14456. The work includes field surveying, installation of new drainage tile, connection to existing drainage infrastructure, installation of drainage outlets and rodent guards, and use of specialized equipment to install drainage tile within vineyard and specialty crop research fields. These improvements are needed to reduce waterlogged conditions, improve soil drainage and field access, increase the amount of usable agricultural land, and support plant genetic resource conservation, regeneration, and agricultural research activities conducted at the facility. This project is essential to support the mission of the United States Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service, Plant Genetic Resources Unit by ensuring that agricultural research and germplasm regeneration fields remain accessible, productive, and suitable for crop production. The installation and improvement of subsurface drainage systems will reduce standing water and waterlogged soil conditions that currently limit planting, cultivation, maintenance, and harvesting operations. If this project is completed, poorly drained areas will continue to experience excessive soil moisture, resulting in reduced field accessibility, delayed planting and harvest operations, increased soil compaction, and degraded growing conditions. These conditions will negatively impact germplasm regeneration activities, research trials, and field-based plant breeding programs by reducing crop establishment, increasing the risk of crop loss, and compromising the quality and reliability of research data. Failure to complete the drainage improvements will also reduce the amount of usable agricultural land available for research and regeneration activities, limiting the Plant Genetic Resources Unit's capacity to maintain, regenerate, and distribute plant genetic resources. Continued deterioration of drainage conditions may result in increased maintenance costs, additional crop losses, and long-term reductions in operational efficiency. The project is therefore mission essential to maintaining critical agricultural research infrastructure and supporting the conservation and utilization of plant genetic resources entrusted to the Agricultural Research Service.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT: THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OR REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL BUT FOR INFORMATIONAL AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY! This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost in developing information provided to the Government. If a solicitation is issued, it will be announced at a later date and all interested parties must respond to that solicitation announcement separately from responses to this announcement. This Sources Sought is only intended to identify potential sources for the purpose of market research, describes only the current contemplated scope of potential requirements and may vary from the scope of the requirement in a final PWS included in any RFQ. The Sources Sought number is 26-P-0000 039061 and shall be used to reference any written responses to this Sources Sought. The anticipated North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code is 481219, Other Nonscheduled Air Transportation with a size standard for the proposed NAICS of $25M. Business Status: The Government is interested in all Small Businesses that are capable of meeting this requirement, including, HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, VOSB, and general Small Businesses. The contractor shall provide a fully mission-capable chase aircraft, along with a qualified pilot and observer crew, to accompany the RPA during all phases of flight outside of restricted airspace. This includes takeoff, traffic pattern operations, transit along established routes, and recovery. The chase crew is responsible for uninterrupted visual scanning, collision avoidance, maintaining communication with both the RPA and Air Traffic Control (ATC), Contractor-Furnished Aircraft & Equipment Requirements Performance: Capable of a sustained speed of 150 knots true airspeed at an altitude of 12,000 feet and below. Communication: Equipped with radios capable of communicating on two separate frequencies simultaneously (one for RPA inter-plane, one for ATC). Insurance & Liability: All chase aircraft shall be fully insured. The Contractor is solely responsible for damages to the aircraft or personnel. Absent Government negligence, the Government shall not be held liable for any damages sustained by the contractor. Onboard Equipment: Chase and RPA will operate beacons and strobe lights during both day and night operations. General Flight Operations Takeoff & Transit: The chase aircraft shall be overhead March ARB (KRIV) at the scheduled RPA takeoff time. The chase will accompany the RPA during pattern operations and transit to restricted airspace (R-2515 or R-2503) per the current COA and LOA. After drop-off, the chase will return to base and remain on standby. Recovery: The chase aircraft will report to the designated pick-up point (R-2515 or R-2503) 10 minutes prior to the scheduled handover time and orbit. Upon clearance, the chase will rejoin the RPA and escort it back to KRIV, remaining in formation until the RPA completes a full-stop landing. Transfer of Control: The chase will maintain visual responsibility until the RPA enters the KRIV traffic pattern and a ground observer officially takes over visual responsibilities. Contractor Personnel & Qualifications General: Only pilots and observers submitted in the contractor's proposal may be used. Any changes or substitutions require prior written approval from the Ordering Officer. Resumes for all personnel must be submitted to the Government. Crew Composition: Standard operations require one (1) chase-qualified pilot and one (1) chase-qualified observer. Two (2) qualified chase pilots are required when oxygen use is mandated by FAA regulations. Crew Responsibilities: Chase Pilot: Responsible for aircraft control and visual separation with the RPA. Chase Observer: Responsible for clearing for traffic and advising the RPA of potential conflicts or deteriorating weather. Pilot Qualifications: Must hold all certifications, ratings, and endorsements required by 14 CFR to act as Pilot in Command. Possess a current airman medical certificate (FAA Class 2 or military equivalent) per 14 CFR 67. Must be current per 14 CFR 61.56 (Flight Review) and 61.57 (Recent Flight Experience). Shall comply with 14 CFR 91.17 regarding alcohol and drug use. Observer Qualifications: Must have a comprehensive understanding of federal aviation regulations for the operational airspace. Shall not perform crew duties for more than one RPA at a time, nor perform concurrent duties as both a pilot and observer. Possess a valid FAA Class 2 medical certificate per 14 CFR 67. Shall comply with 14 CFR 91.17 regarding alcohol and drug use. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Firms responding to this Sources Sought notice are requested to provide a capability statement. description: Kainuun hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia Holter -palveluista Kainuun keskussairaalaan sisätaudeille ja lastentaudeille sekä Suomussalmen, Kuhmon, Puolangan ja Sotkamon terveysasemille erikoissairaanhoidon toimintana. Justification: The Sonosite LX will provide clinicians with high-quality, real-time bedside imaging necessary for the care of critically ill pediatric patients in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU). The system supports rapid diagnosis and ultrasound-guided procedures, including vascular access, cardiac assessments, pulmonary evaluations, abdominal imaging, and other point-of-care applications. Its portability, exceptional image quality, intuitive touchscreen workflow, advanced needle visualization technology, and comprehensive imaging capabilities enable timely clinical decision-making, improve procedural success, reduce complications, and enhance patient safety. The inclusion of multiple transducers allows a single platform to support a broad range of pediatric and critical care examinations, maximizing clinical utility while minimizing equipment redundancy. The five-year manufacturer warranty and onsite clinical training further ensure long-term reliability and successful implementation. FUJIFILM Sonosite is a recognized industry leader in point-of-care ultrasound technology with extensive experience supporting hospitals and critical care environments. The vendor offers the complete Sonosite LX platform, manufacturer-certified installation, clinical education, technical support, and a comprehensive five-year warranty for both the ultrasound system and transducers. The proposed equipment is available through an existing federal contract, ensuring compliance with federal procurement requirements while providing access to factory-authorized service, software updates, replacement components, and ongoing technical support. As the original equipment manufacturer, FUJIFILM Sonosite is uniquely qualified to provide the equipment, warranty coverage, training, and lifecycle support necessary to maintain safe and reliable operation in the NIH Clinical Center's Pediatric Intensive Care Unit. title: Consultancy: El Niño 2026 Research on Anticipatory Action for Children – Bangladesh and Somalia
description: Summary El Niño 2026 is highly likely to intensify extreme weather, hitting hardest in already fragile, crisis-aƯected contexts. Children will bear the brunt through cascading impacts on health, education, protection, and lifelong well-being, alongside significant and under-recognised loss and damage. This research will generate evidence on how these impacts unfold and how to reduce impacts and loss and damage for children, using El Niño as an entry point to inform more eƯective design, targeting, and scaling of preparedness, anticipatory action (AA) and adaptation. It will examine what works in AA, pinpointing eƯective interventions, and how systems can deliver timely, child-centred responses at scale and contribute to the evidence base for policy, financing and practice on how AA can reduce climate-related risks, losses and damages for children and strengthen resilience to future shocks. Research aim and objectives This research aims to generate actionable, child-centred evidence to inform more eƯective AA, preparedness, adaptation and responses to the 2026/26 El Niño event1 and similar climate shocks. The research is intended to inform programming and decision-making by governments, local and national actors, NGOs, donors and multilateral organisations, while contributing to wider policy and financing discussions on child-centred AA, resilience and loss and damage. It will document the loss and damage experienced by children in the context of El Niño and cumulative shocks and examine how AA can reduce the impacts on children, as well as avert, minimise and address loss and damage. The research is designed as a phased study that reflects both the anticipated progression of El Niño impacts and the time required to assess resilience and adaptation outcomes. Phase I, conducted in 2026, will focus on the immediate impacts of El Niño on children, together with an assessment of the eƯectiveness of anticipatory actions and early responses in reducing risks, losses and damages. While this phase will identify potential pathways to resilience and adaptation, it is not expected to generate suƯicient evidence to assess longer-term resilience outcomes directly. Subject to additional funding, Phase II extending the research beyond 2026, would enable analysis of longer-term and secondary impacts, as well as the contribution of anticipatory action to resilience, adaptive capacity, and vulnerability reduction for children, households and communities. The research seeks to answer the following specific questions: 1. What are the immediate and emerging impacts2 of El Niño on children? a) What impact does El Niño have on children across the most affected sectors in the selected contexts?3 b) What losses and damages do children experience as a result of El Niño and compounding shocks? c) Which children and contexts are at greatest risk? d) How do El Niño impacts interact with other climate, economic and conflict-related stressors? 2. How can anticipatory action effectively reduce the impacts experienced by children (including through actions that are timely, adequately financed, appropriately targeted, inclusive, locally led, and contextually appropriate to reduce risks, losses and damages for children)? 1 Unless otherwise stated, reference to El Niño within this document will refer to the 2026/27 event. 2 We note that impacts of the current El Niño event will extend into 2027 and in many instances may not be fully felt until considerably later. 3 Sectors could include, for example, health, education, protection and well-being; given the scope of the study, it may, however, be necessary to focus on those sectors most significantly aƯected by El Niño in the chosen geographic context, and where suƯicient relevant data is available to support meaningful analysis. 4 a) Which AA actions, modalities, and interventions are effective in mitigating negative impacts and loss and damage for children? b) What governance, coordination/capacity factors enable or constrain national and local actors in leading/sustaining effective anticipatory action? c) Which children benefit the most from interventions (e.g. age, gender, vulnerability)? d) What affects – or constrains – the effectiveness of interventions and how do these vary across contexts? e) How do different components of AA systems, including risk analysis, early warning, trigger mechanisms, pre-agreed action plans, financing, targeting and delivery, interact to shape outcomes for children? What are the key bottlenecks that constrain the timeliness, adequacy, inclusiveness, effectiveness and scale of AA? 3. (Second phase, subject to extension of research)4 : How do the impacts of El Niño evolve over time, and to what extent does anticipatory action contribute to reduced vulnerability, resilience and strengthened adaptation capacity for children, households and communities? a) To what extent do the impacts, losses and damages associated with El Niño persist beyond the initial shock period? b) What secondary and longer-term consequences emerge for children across education, health, protection, wellbeing and livelihoods? c) To what extent, and through what pathways, does AA contribute to longer-term adaptive capacity and resilience for children, households and communities? d) What lessons can inform the integration of anticipatory action, adaptation and longer-term development programming?

title: Germany – Fibre-optic connections – Glasfaser
description: Zur Verbesserung der Wohnqualität sowie zur Steigerung der Attraktivität für die Studierenden sollen die Wohnanlagen mit modernen Glasfaser-Internet Anbindungen versehen werden. Zudem soll ein hochverfügbarer und performanter WLAN-Zugang für die Wohneinheiten sowie Teile der gemeinschaftlich genutzten Bereiche eingerichtet werden. Mit dieser Beschaffungsmaßnahme soll ein Auftragnehmer (nachfolgend "Auftragnehmer" genannt) für den Internet-Service der Wohnanlagen des Auftraggebers ausgewählt werden. Der ausgeschriebene Leistungsumfang umfasst die Lieferung, Installation und betriebsbereite Übergabe einer Gesamtlösung, bestehend aus WLAN-Komponenten, aktiven LAN-Switches, Endgeräten (Routern), sowie Breitband-Internet-Zugängen auf Basis von symmetrischen Glasfaseranbindungen. Nach erfolgreicher Inbetriebnahme übernimmt der Auftragnehmer den Betrieb des Internet-Services für sämtliche Wohnanlagen und stellt während der gesamten Vertragslaufzeit die Verfügbarkeit sowie die einwandfreie Funktionalität der Dienste und Infrastruktur sicher. Hierzu zählt auch die Instandhaltung der passiven Netzwerkinfrastruktur. Die Bereitstellung des Dienstes erfolgt abschnittsweise ab dem 1. Januar 2027.
